solution: \(g\circ f(x)=g(x^2-1)=x-\sqrt{x}+1\). Substitute \(t=x^2-1\), so \(x=\sqrt{t+1}\) (taking \(x\ge 0\)): \(g(t)=\sqrt{t+1}-\sqrt{\sqrt{t+1}}+1=\sqrt{t+1}-\sqrt[4]{t+1}+1\). Hence \(g(x)=\sqrt{x+1}-\sqrt[4]{x+1}+1\), which is option B. Common mistake: not performing the substitution to find \(g\) explicitly, or dropping the \(+1\).
